use_case_name: Decorrelate Diverging Air or Surface Tracks

evidence_cards.content: The goal is to prevent or eliminate dual designations by comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the objective of the correlation process, which serves as the high-level goal for the use case involving track management.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the high-level objective for the C2 JU: to avoid automatic correlation under specified diverging track conditions, which directly supports the 'goal' slot of the use case 'Decorrelate Diverging Air or Surface Tracks'.

evidence_cards.content: The goal of the use case is to decorrelate any two air tracks or any two surface tracks.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.4.3.2 AIR AND SURFACE TRACK DECORRELATION, first paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the high-level objective of the process described in the section, which matches the definition of the 'goal' slot.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to resolve dual designations when two tracks are recognized as eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the high-level goal of the use case: resolving dual designations through correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The high-level objective is to decorrelate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN when they are subjected to decorrelation criteria.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the primary action and intent of the use case: separating two specific track numbers.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory system capability (automatic correlation) that must exist before the decorrelation use case can be invoked, as it implies the precondition of having correlated tracks to potentially diverge.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks; or (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These restrictions define the system state where automatic correlation is inhibited. For the 'Decorrelate' use case, these specific states serve as preconditions indicating that the tracks are currently in a restricted mode or have diverged significantly enough to warrant separation/non-correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically select as the TN to be dropped a TN which has any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a constraint on track selection that must hold before decorrelation can proceed; it is a precondition for the use case execution.

evidence_cards.content: In the absence of such a selection constraint, JUs shall select the higher TN as the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies default behavior if no OCC constraints apply — this is part of the pre-decision logic required before initiating decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: For a track that has both a TN greater than 07777 and a TN less than 07777, as reported in a J7.4 message, the track with TN greater than 07777 shall be used in this comparison.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines how to resolve ambiguous TN values prior to selecting which track to drop — a necessary condition for consistent decorrelation initiation.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that initiate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic decorrelation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the necessary system state and capability (automatic decorrelation) required for the primary actor before the use case can be executed.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the system state (recognition of dual designation) required before the resolution process can begin.

evidence_cards.content: The Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system state condition where tracks are subject to decorrelation criteria, which serves as a precondition for the rejection logic described in the subsequent text.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated if the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the specific system state condition (meeting decorrelation criteria) that must hold before the C2 JU can initiate the decorrelation action described in the use case.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation testing shall consist of the position, velocity, and altitude tests specified in this paragraph.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state (tests) that must be performed as part of the correlation process before decorrelation can occur.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a strict timing constraint for the correlation tests, which is a condition of the system state.

evidence_cards.content: A local track shall be considered to correlate to the closest remote track or IU that meets all of the correlation tests...
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the successful state of correlation (meeting all tests) which serves as the baseline context for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These are explicit system state conditions that must hold before automatic correlation is restricted — directly defining preconditions under which decorrelation behavior (or inhibition of correlation) applies.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit this automatic restriction for ID conflicts or differing Mode II codes, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C² IUs.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This identifies the specific condition (existence of two eligible tracks meeting decorrelation criteria) that initiates the decorrelation process.

evidence_cards.content: The restrictions do not apply to manual correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies that the trigger applies only to automatic correlation; manual decorrelation may be initiated independently by an operator.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific system event (receipt of J2/J3 message) that triggers the automatic testing process leading to decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: The use case is triggered when a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly defines the event (recognition of eligibility) that initiates the action sequence described in the text.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This identifies the specific triggering event — receipt of a J7.2 message with RV=3 — that initiates automatic correlation acceptance (which is the inverse or complementary action to decorrelation; however, since the use case is 'Decorrelate Diverging Tracks', this may represent an exception path where decorrelation is blocked). For trigger extraction, it defines the system event that starts processing related to track correlation status, which can lead to decorrelation if restrictions apply.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: While not the primary trigger for decorrelation, this describes a user-facing consequence (operator alert) triggered by rejection of correlation — which may be part of the broader context leading to manual decorrelation initiation. However, it does not directly define the start of the 'Decorrelate' use case itself.

evidence_cards.content: If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the first action step of the main flow: performing the actual decorrelation operation when divergence conditions are met.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, the C2 JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the immediate follow-up action after decorrelation — initiating a new track report, which is part of the canonical success scenario.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies required field values in the post-decorrelation report, completing the interaction sequence for successful decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: A new local track that correlates with another track on each of the first two correlation tests shall be correlated and held as a common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system’s automatic response to successful correlation during initial testing — establishing a 'common local track' state, which is a key step in the main flow before potential decorrelation triggers occur later.

evidence_cards.content: Thereafter, the decorrelation rules (see paragraph 4.4.4.3.2) apply to the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Explicitly links the establishment of a common local track to the subsequent application of decorrelation rules — indicating that decorrelation is a follow-on process triggered after correlation success, forming part of the canonical sequence for managing diverging tracks.

evidence_cards.content: After it has been determined that a common local track (TN A) satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation, the local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the first step in the execution sequence (main flow) after the trigger criteria are met.

evidence_cards.content: If the automatic correlation test fails, the system assigns a new TN (TN B) to the local track and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the second step in the main flow: the action taken upon failure of the re-correlation test to finalize the decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU receives a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection), it shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system response and timing constraint following a correlation rejection, which is a key step in the decorrelation workflow.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the automatic acceptance logic for manually initiated correlations, establishing the baseline behavior before potential decorrelation triggers.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a post-condition/time-out period preventing immediate automatic decorrelation after a manual correlation is established.

evidence_cards.content: If the received RV field is set to value 0 and there is an OCC on the Dropped TN, the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details a specific conditional branch in the main flow where the system responds to a correlation request by initiating a reverse correlation based on Operational Control Code (OCC) status.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C2 JU has R-squared, the C2 JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This claim provides the specific execution step for dropping a track when the local unit retains responsibility ($R^2$) but receives conflicting PPLI data.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, the C2 JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This claim defines the final system state action (creating a new track) following the detection of decorrelation criteria.

evidence_cards.content: The Velocity Test requires that the reported course of the remote track shall be within f degrees of the calculated course of the local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific step in the main flow where the system evaluates track divergence based on course difference to determine if decorrelation is required.

evidence_cards.content: The speed of the slower track shall be within g percent of the speed of the faster track, or within g*200/S_F percent for air tracks or g*20/S_F percent for surface tracks, whichever is greater.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the speed comparison criteria used in the main flow to assess whether tracks are diverging sufficiently to warrant decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: Velocity comparisons shall use the last reported course and speed of remote tracks and the course and speed calculated for local tracks at the common time to which the tracks are extrapolated at the time of comparison.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the temporal alignment method used during the velocity test step in the main flow, ensuring accurate comparison between local and remote track data.

evidence_cards.content: If the Altitude Source of both air tracks is either 1 (Sensor) or 3 (Aircraft Automatic Altitude Report), or if the local track Altitude Source is 1 or 3 and the remote track is an IU reported in a PPLI message, the altitude differential between the two tracks shall not be greater than h.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a conditional step in the main flow where altitude differential is evaluated as part of the decorrelation criteria for air tracks.

evidence_cards.content: If the Altitude Source of either track is 0 (No Statement/Estimated) or 2 (Aircraft Report), Altitude shall not be used in the correlation test.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an exception condition within the main flow where altitude data is excluded from evaluation, affecting how the decorrelation decision is made.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) Identity (ID) difference constituting a conflict; (2) different Mode II codes with local Mode II code current; (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data; or (4) either track has Strength field set to value greater than 1 (except when set to No Statement).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines automatic correlation restrictions that prevent decorrelation under specific divergence conditions — directly constraining the main flow by specifying when automatic decorrelation is inhibited.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and operator selectable capability to inhibit automatic restriction for ID conflicts or Mode II mismatches, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C² IUs via voice or other communications media; in lieu of specific direction, all IUs restrict automatic correlation by default.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies configurable override mechanisms for automatic correlation restrictions — affects whether main flow proceeds automatically or requires manual intervention.

evidence_cards.content: The local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks) in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the first explicit execution step in the main flow after decorrelation criteria are met — it defines the system’s immediate action upon triggering decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: If the automatic correlation test fails, assign a new TN (TN B) to the local track and report TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the concrete system response and message transmission required upon failure of the correlation test — fulfilling the evidence aspect for 'execution steps for dropping the track' via message reporting.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU may elect to accept changes in Environment/Category, Identity or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific interaction step where the actor resolves differences by accepting remote data under strict conditions (Friend vs. non-Hostile).

evidence_cards.content: When accepting a remote ID change, C2 JUs shall retain the received values of Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields for retransmission and operator appreciation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the system state update action required after resolving an ID difference.

evidence_cards.content: Differences in Environment/Category, ID, Platform, etc., may be resolved with the use of the J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific execution step for reporting a decorrelation outcome (rejection), which is a critical part of the interaction sequence for dropping or rejecting a track association.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the specific execution step for dropping a track after correlation processing, which is part of the main flow interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall be transmitted after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the sequential ordering of message transmissions required to complete the decorrelation process.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines specific constraints on manual correlation that act as alternative paths diverging from standard decorrelation procedures; these restrictions prevent successful manual correlation under certain conditions, which constitutes an alternative flow where the system must handle tracks differently than in the main automatic decorrelation scenario.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the automatic correlation process is restricted/blocked due to ID conflict, preventing the standard decorrelation or correlation path.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the automatic correlation process is restricted/blocked due to Mode II mismatch, preventing the standard decorrelation or correlation path.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the automatic correlation process is restricted/blocked because both tracks are local, preventing the standard decorrelation or correlation path.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1, unless the Strength is set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the automatic correlation process is restricted/blocked based on the Strength field value, preventing the standard decorrelation or correlation path.

evidence_cards.content: If the above actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test shall be conducted only once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative path where ID conflict is resolved via voice coordination or restriction confirmation, followed by a one-time decorrelation test before correlation — diverging from the main flow’s automatic decorrelation upon divergence detection.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically select as the TN to be dropped a TN which has any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7). In the absence of such a selection constraint, JUs shall select the higher TN as the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative rule for Track Number selection during decorrelation that overrides the default 'drop higher TN' behavior when specific Operational Control Codes are present — representing a variant execution path within the decorrelation process.

evidence_cards.content: For a track that has both a TN greater than 07777 and a TN less than 07777, as reported in a J7.4 message, the track with TN greater than 07777 shall be used in this comparison.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an alternative handling rule for dual-TN tracks in J7.4 messages, affecting which TN is selected for dropping — a conditional branch in the decorrelation logic that alters the standard selection procedure.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request and all associated processing for the correlation shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative outcome path where correlation fails due to timeout, leading to cancellation — a successful termination of the decorrelation attempt under failure conditions, distinct from the canonical success scenario.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN shall be designated as a common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Represents an alternative disposition path for the Dropped TN based on local track ownership status — diverging from the general case by assigning a specific designation (common local track) to the retained track.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted for the Dropped TN. If the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after transmission of the J7.0, own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details an alternative flow triggered by presence of R² data: explicit drop message transmission followed by temporary lockout against re-correlation — a structured recovery/continuation path differing from immediate decorrelation completion.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the Target or Reference TN of a J10.2 Engagement Status message, C2 JU shall decorrelate and alert an operator as a cue to transmit the J10.2 message with the Weapon Engagement Status field set to value 8 (Engagement Broken) if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path triggered by active engagement status, requiring operator intervention to update engagement messages rather than immediate automatic reporting of the new track.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message which own unit originated or is preparing a reply, C2 JU shall execute the decorrelation and provide operator display of new track status on TNs A and B before release of the J9.0 reply.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path where decorrelation occurs but is gated by the need to display status to the operator before releasing a pending command reply relative to the original TN A.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is controlled by own unit (subject of J10.5 Controlling Unit Report), C2 JU shall not automatically decorrelate; if manually decorrelated, it must alert the operator to report termination of control on TN A.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path that inhibits automatic decorrelation for controlled tracks, requiring manual initiation and subsequent reporting of control termination.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A has been paired by own unit (subject of J10.6 message), C2 JU shall decorrelate and alert an operator as a cue to terminate the pairing on TN A and initiate the pairing on TN B if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path for paired tracks, requiring operator action to transfer the pairing relationship from the old track number to the new one.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held and the Dropped TN has an OCC, C2 JU transmits a reverse correlation with RV set to 1 if the received RV is 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative successful path (reverse correlation) when the receiving unit holds the dropped track under specific conditions.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held and the Dropped TN has an OCC, C2 JU executes the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number if the received RV is 3.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative successful path where the roles are effectively swapped due to local track holdings.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held and the Dropped TN does not have an OCC, C2 JU executes the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative successful path for executing correlation based on local track availability.

evidence_cards.content: A manual capability shall be provided to initiate the correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the correlation test criteria in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f, the correlation restrictions in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g, or the requirements in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1h.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where manual intervention overrides automatic correlation rules, allowing decorrelation even when standard tests would permit correlation.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies constraints on the manual override alternative flow — certain track combinations remain ineligible for manual correlation despite the general override capability.

evidence_cards.content: If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed (exception to restrictions).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific legal alternative path where automatic correlation is permitted despite restrictions, effectively allowing the system to proceed with correlation rather than decorrelation under these specific ID conditions.

evidence_cards.content: Under this exception, the Unknown/Hostile track shall be designated as the dropped Track Number (TN-2), which allows breaking the engagement and/or destroying missile(s) in flight.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the outcome of the alternative flow: the system resolves the dual designation by dropping the hostile track while maintaining the friend track, diverging from the standard restriction that would block correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the Target TN of a J10.2 Engagement Status message for a current engagement reported and conducted by own unit, or is the Reference TN or Target TN of a J10.2 message for a current engagement reported by own unit and conducted by another unit, C2 JU shall decorrelate and alert an operator as a cue to transmit the J10.2 message with the Weapon Engagement Status field set to value 8 (Engagement Broken) if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific alternative flow where decorrelation is triggered by active engagement status messages, diverging from the standard automatic test failure trigger.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message which own unit originated or to which own unit is preparing a reply, C2 JU shall execute the decorrelation and provide operator display of new track status on TNs A and B before release of the J9.0 reply.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative flow handling decorrelation during pending command replies, ensuring the reply is relative to TN A only.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is controlled by own unit (subject of J10.5 Controlling Unit Report), C2 JU shall not automatically decorrelate; if manually decorrelated, it must alert the operator to report termination of control of TN A if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an alternative flow preventing automatic decorrelation when the track is under own unit control, requiring manual intervention and reporting.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A has been paired by own unit (subject of J10.6 message), C2 JU shall decorrelate and alert an operator as a cue to terminate the pairing on TN A and initiate the pairing on TN B if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details an alternative flow for breaking existing pairings upon decorrelation, shifting the pairing relationship to the new track.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A has been correlated with an Index Number by own unit (subject of J12.5 message), C2 JU shall assess whether the Index Number should remain with TN A or B, and transmit J12.5 messages as appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Outlines an alternative flow involving the reassignment or retention of index numbers associated with the tracks during decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the subject of a handover in progress (TN in a J10.3 Handover message), decorrelation shall be delayed until the handover process is completed or terminated, then executed with an operator alert to report control in the J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where decorrelation is temporally suspended due to an ongoing handover process.

evidence_cards.content: If the C² JU has correlated local sensor data for the track obtained via a J12.6 Target Sorting message from a nonC² JU, the paragraph regarding initial TQ assignment need not be applied with regard to TQ.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative condition where the standard reporting procedure (assigning TQ based on Table 4.4-7) is bypassed if local correlation exists, representing a divergence in the flow of handling received tracks.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall automatically set the Identity Amplifying Descriptor to Exercise Friend for all tracks in their database which have the Exercise Indicator set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative successful flow path where track identity is explicitly modified to 'Exercise Friend' upon receiving a specific exercise status order, diverging from standard decorrelation or correlation behaviors.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall automatically set all data fields that may contain artificial information to the No Statement, default value, or actual values if held in database, and set the Exercise Indicator to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative flow for clearing artificial data and resetting the Exercise Indicator, representing a successful variant of track management distinct from the main decorrelation flow.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall break any locally originated engagement involving the TN by transmitting a J10.2 (WES = 8) message to report the engagement broken.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an alternative successful action (breaking engagement) triggered by an exercise status order, which diverts from the main flow of track maintenance or correlation.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall terminate any locally originated Command message with Command values 2, 3, 5, or 7 involving the TN, by transmitting a J9.0 message with the Command field set to value 4 (Cease Engage) or value 5 (Hold Fire), if the Engagement Status field is set to value 4 (Firing).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details an alternative successful flow for terminating active commands during an exercise reset, representing a valid divergence from normal operational flows when under exercise control.

evidence_cards.content: If the Reference TN is being reported in a J3.7 message, the reporting JU shall transmit all data held in a J3.7 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow for responding to data update requests specifically when the track is reported via a J3.7 message, diverging from the standard response logic.

evidence_cards.content: If the request is collectively addressed, any JU which has initiated an EW evaluation or association on the Reference TN in a J14.2 message shall transmit a J14.2 message with EW Action Value field set to values 7, 8, or 9 addressed to the requesting unit with the R/C field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative flow path triggered by a 'collectively addressed' request involving Electronic Warfare (EW) evaluations, requiring specific field values in the response message.

evidence_cards.content: If the request is specifically addressed, the addressee shall transmit all locally held EW evaluations and associations in the J14.2 message with EW Action Value field set to values 7, 8, or 9.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow for 'specifically addressed' requests, differing from the collective address scenario in terms of who responds and how the data is transmitted.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception flow where the system detects a conflict (different TNs for same track) and responds by transmitting a rejection message rather than automatically merging or dropping tracks unilaterally.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception handling path where conflicting data sources (PPLI vs J3) exist for the same track; the system resolves this by prioritizing PPLI unless quality is zero.

evidence_cards.content: In the case where Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0 during a same-TN correlation conflict, the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the fallback behavior within the exception flow when the primary resolution (accepting PPLI) fails due to poor data quality.

evidence_cards.content: If an operator action has been taken which selectively released a new local track for reporting, it shall be transmitted, regardless of the results of correlation testing.

source_locations.location: Section b. New Local Tracks, last sentence

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception flow where standard automatic correlation rules (and potential decorrelation outcomes) are bypassed by explicit operator intervention to force transmission.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.

source_locations.location: paragraph g. Correlation Restrictions, items (1) through (4)

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These are explicit exception conditions that prevent automatic correlation — directly defining the exception_flow for the decorrelate diverging tracks use case by specifying when automatic correlation must be inhibited.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction for ID conflicts or Mode II code mismatches, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C² IUs; if no specific interface direction exists, all IUs will restrict automatic correlation by default.

source_locations.location: paragraph g.(1) and g.(2), parenthetical notes

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines configurable override mechanisms for exceptions — part of exception handling flow where operators can bypass restrictions under coordinated conditions, otherwise default behavior applies.

evidence_cards.content: The restrictions do not apply to manual correlation. No other correlation restrictions shall be applied for two tracks which pass the correlation tests specified in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f.

source_locations.location: paragraph g. Correlation Restrictions, second sentence

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies scope of exception_flow: these restrictions only block *automatic* correlation; manual correlation remains permitted, and no additional restrictions apply beyond those listed — critical boundary for exception handling logic.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request and all associated processing for the correlation shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an explicit exception flow where the correlation process fails due to a timeout condition, resulting in the cancellation of processing.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN shall be designated as a common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific exception handling path for the disposition of the Dropped Track Number based on the current state of the 'own unit' (holding it as a local/common local track).

evidence_cards.content: If own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted; if the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after transmission, own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details an alternative/exception flow involving the transmission of a drop message and a subsequent lockout period preventing re-correlation if the track is reported externally.

evidence_cards.content: If the automatic correlation test fails during decorrelation execution, C2 JU assigns a new TN (TN B) to the local track and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the system's recovery action upon failure of the automatic correlation test — a key exception flow where the primary path (correlation success) is not taken, triggering an alternative assignment and reporting mechanism.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system response (assume R²) to an unexpected condition (receipt of Drop Track message) where the actor retains responsibility for the track.

evidence_cards.content: Immediately prior to assuming R² for an air or surface track after receipt of a Drop Track message, a JU shall test the track for correlation in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g, except the test shall be conducted only once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a mandatory validation step (correlation test) required before resolving the exception state.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the state of the system initiating a new track as a result of the decorrelation process.

evidence_cards.content: In the post-decorrelation surveillance track report, the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exact data values required in the system state following successful decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: If the automatic correlation test fails during decorrelation execution, C2 JU assigns a new Track Number (TN B) to the local track and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the final system state after successful decorrelation: a new TN is assigned and reported, indicating the tracks are now treated as separate entities.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number, reporting the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field as No Statement.

source_locations.location: Page 4-180, paragraph g(2) and implied by context of J3.2/J3.3 reporting

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the content and format of the post-decorrelation report, confirming the system has successfully separated the tracks and is reporting them independently with specific field values.

evidence_cards.content: After the decorrelation is executed and the automatic correlation test fails, C2 JU assigns a new Track Number (TN B) to the local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the resulting system state regarding the track identity after successful decorrelation execution, fulfilling the postcondition of the track being re-identified.

evidence_cards.content: Following the assignment of the new Track Number (TN B), C2 JU reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This confirms the final observable action/state where the system communicates the new track status to external units, marking the completion of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the immediate system state change after successful decorrelation: initiation of a new track report with a new TN, which is a direct postcondition of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: In that report, C2 JU reports the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exact field values set in the newly initiated track report after decorrelation — this defines part of the observable post-state of the system following successful completion.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific post-success state constraint (lockout period) following a successful manual correlation resolution within the use case scope.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system state and required user interaction (alert/cue) following a rejection event in the manual flow.
